title: Birth and Death Certificate Correction in Bangladesh for NRBs: Online Process and Court Route
metaTitle: Birth & Death Certificate Correction in Bangladesh for NRBs
metaDescription: How to correct name, date of birth or parents' names on a Bangladesh birth or death certificate from abroad: BDRIS online correction, documents, appeals and court options.
heroIntro: A tiny spelling error in a birth certificate can block a visa, citizenship or inheritance matter. NRBs are especially affected because documents from different systems must match: passport, NID, school records and foreign applications. This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Correction in Brief
points: Birth and death registration is governed by the Births and Deaths Registration Act 2004.
Corrections are normally applied for through the online BDRIS system at the Registrar's office (City Corporation, Pourashava or Union Parishad).
Minor errors in spelling are easier to fix than date of birth or parents' identity.
Supporting documents are essential: school certificates, hospital records, NID, passport and parents' documents.
If the Registrar refuses, appeal to the higher authority or approach the court.

sections.content:
• Spelling mistakes in the name.
  • Wrong date of birth or place.
  • Wrong parents' names or NID numbers.
  • Mismatch between the Bangla and English versions.
  • Name changed after marriage or conversion not reflected.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

1. Open the official birth and death registration portal (BDRIS) and find your registration number.
  2. Fill in the correction application and select the field to be corrected.
  3. Upload supporting documents: old certificate, NID/passport, school certificates, parents' ID, hospital record.
  4. Pay the correction fee online.
  5. The Registrar reviews the application, may call for a hearing, and issues the corrected certificate.

NRBs can apply online and let a relative or attorney attend if a hearing is needed.

• Oldest school certificate (SSC or primary) showing the correct date of birth.
  • Vaccination card or hospital discharge certificate.
  • Parents' NID and marriage certificate.
  • Passport and NID of the applicant.
  • Affidavit sworn before a Magistrate or Notary stating the correct details.

If the Registrar rejects the application, you can appeal to the authority specified in the Act (generally the Deputy Commissioner or the Director General of the registration authority) within the time limit given in the rejection order. For serious disputes, such as changing the date of birth by a large margin or parentage, a civil suit for declaration may be needed. An advocate can advise on the best route.

Death certificates are needed for heirship certificates, mutation and bank claims. Errors in the deceased's name or date can delay inheritance. Correct them using the same online process, and make sure the deceased's name matches the land records (see inheritance guide).

1. Fix errors before applying for visas or citizenship abroad.
  2. Keep the name consistent across passport, NID and certificates.
  3. Use certified English translations for foreign authorities and attest them (see attestation guide).
  4. Do not use touts; use official portals and receipts.
  5. Ask your advocate for an affidavit if documents conflict.

faqs.question: Can I correct a birth certificate from abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the online BDRIS system, with a relative or advocate attending any hearing.

faqs.question: Can I change my date of birth in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Small corrections with strong evidence can be made administratively; large changes may require a court order.

faqs.question: What documents are needed for correction?
faqs.answer: Old certificate, school records, NID/passport, parents' documents and an affidavit if needed.

faqs.question: How long does correction take?
faqs.answer: It varies by office, from a few weeks to months, depending on the case.

faqs.question: Can I correct a death certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the same process; supporting documents of the deceased are needed.
